constraints: SQLite remains the canonical fact store; FTS and graph tables are rebuildable projections.
Consolidation is deterministic by default and never gives an LLM direct stable-card write authority.
Candidate and card history is append-only; stale, superseded, rejected, and uncertain states remain queryable.
Only visible user, assistant, tool, command, file, and validation records may be imported; hidden reasoning and credentials are not persisted.
The complete local history export is processed outside the repository and is not committed as a raw archive.
No embedding/vector dependency, graph database, or private Codex database mutation is introduced in this slice.
data.goal: Deliver the next coding-memory vertical slice: promote evidence-backed extraction candidates into versioned memory cards with relations and lifecycle states, add deterministic consolidation and inspection APIs/CLI, and ingest all locally indexed visible Codex history through a bounded replay path.
non_goals: AST/LSP or live CodebaseMemory symbol verification (Phase 4).
Production MCP server and native Codex Desktop hook (Phase 5/7).
data.stop_condition: Stop after the card consolidation/lifecycle vertical slice, bounded complete-history import and extraction smoke, API/CLI/UI projection updates, regression verification, and explicit recording of remaining Phase 4+ gaps.
success_criteria: Candidate rows remain immutable and can be consolidated idempotently into versioned cards with evidence, aliases, bindings, and auditable relation links.
Repeated observations merge without duplicate cards; changed bindings or contradictory observations create explicit versions/relations rather than silently overwriting history.
Every stable or proposed card is traceable to at least one canonical event and every stored binding retains its source evidence ids.
The importer can process the complete local Codex history export in bounded batches, preserve thread/cwd/source/completeness provenance, and safely replay duplicates.
Card listing, detail, history, relations, consolidation, and graph projection are available through the service layer, CLI, and REST API.
Existing tests plus new consolidation, lifecycle, bulk-history, API, and integrity tests pass; malformed provider data and failed consolidation do not damage canonical events or prior card versions.
